name: Business Weight (Feature 4)
description: Add business_weight float to Context/WorkerNode. Compute from signal frequency, author seniority (from identity resolver), channel gravity (learned from response patterns), engagement velocity. Use for token budget allocation per context and routing priority. Default 0.5, floor 0.1, range [0.0, 1.0]. Layered across data model, computation, and routing integration modules. Raw vs effective weight distinction: raw is the computed weighted average in [0.0, 1.0], effective is max(raw, policy_floor) in [0.1, 1.0]. Frozen result objects for safe sharing across async boundaries. Configurable metric weights (normalized internally, need not sum to 1.0). Graceful degradation on missing inputs (default to 0.5 neutral sentinel). Proportional token budget allocation with largest-remainder rounding. Integration with existing BFS stop-on-first-accept routing as a priority bias (affects evaluation ORDER only, never acceptance criteria).

functions.name: compute_business_weight_from_metrics
functions.description: Pure synchronous function that computes a BusinessWeightResult from BusinessWeightMetrics using a weighted average formula. Formula: raw = clamp((w_sf * signal_frequency + w_as * author_seniority + w_cg * channel_gravity + w_ev * engagement_velocity) / sum_of_weights, 0.0, 1.0). Returns both raw and effective (floor-applied) weights. If all config weights are zero, returns default 0.5 as raw weight. This function has NO side effects — it does not mutate metrics or context. Located in the data model layer (primitives/ or core/).

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Configuration controlling weights, floor, and defaults.

error_data.field: name of the invalid config field

config.policy_floor is in [0.0, 1.0]

functions.name: resolve_business_weight
functions.description: Async wrapper that resolves all sub-metric inputs from external dependencies and signal history, then delegates to compute_business_weight_from_scores(). Fetches author seniority from the identity resolver with a configurable timeout and fallback to default. Computes signal_frequency by counting signals in the time window normalized by frequency_saturation. Computes engagement_velocity from the rate of change of signal volume across window halves. Looks up channel_gravity from learned channel weights map. Returns the full BusinessWeightComponents for observability. Does NOT mutate context.business_weight — the caller (lifecycle check) is responsible for assignment. Located in core/business_weight.py.

functions.description: Pure helper function that computes the engagement velocity from signal history. Splits the time window into two halves, counts signals in each half, and computes the rate of change as (recent_count - older_count) / max(older_count, 1), squashed through a sigmoid-like function to [0.0, 1.0].

functions.name: allocate_token_budget
functions.description: Distributes a total token budget across contexts proportionally by business_weight using a floor-then-proportional algorithm with largest-remainder rounding. Algorithm: (a) Compute minimum floor allocation per context. (b) If sum of floor allocations exceeds total_budget, apply pro-rata reduction. (c) Distribute the remainder proportionally by business_weight. (d) Use largest-remainder method (Hare quota) for integer rounding so the sum of allocated_tokens equals total_budget exactly. This is a pure function.

error_cases.condition: Sum of all business_weights is 0.0 (should not happen with floor of 0.1, but guarded)

error_data.message: Total business_weight sum is 0.0; cannot compute proportional allocation

preconditions: total_budget >= 0
len(contexts) >= 1
All contexts have valid business_weight values (in [0.1, 1.0] after validation)
All context_ids are unique within the input list
postconditions: len(result) == len(contexts)
sum(a.allocated_tokens for a in result) == total_budget
for all a in result: a.allocated_tokens >= 0
for all a in result: a.proportion >= 0.0 and a.proportion <= 1.0
sum(a.proportion for a in result) is approximately 1.0 (within floating-point epsilon) when total_budget > 0
Each result element's context_id matches exactly one input context's context_id
Each result element's business_weight equals the corresponding input context's business_weight
If total_budget == 0, all allocated_tokens are 0 and all proportions are 0.0
If all contexts have equal business_weight, all allocations are equal (within +/- 1 token due to rounding)

functions.name: compute_business_weight_from_inputs
functions.description: Computes a business weight from four normalized input signals: signal frequency, author seniority, channel gravity, and engagement velocity. Returns a clamped value in [0.1, 1.0]. This is a pure function consumed by Context construction upstream — it is NOT part of the routing/budget execution path. Consumers of routing and budget functions receive pre-computed weights. Located in the routing integration layer.

inputs.name: seniority
inputs.description: Author seniority score from identity resolver, normalized to [0.0, 1.0].

inputs.name: gravity
inputs.description: Channel gravity learned from response patterns, normalized to [0.0, 1.0].

error_data.message: All inputs must be finite numbers

preconditions: All inputs are finite floats in [0.0, 1.0]
postconditions: result >= 0.1 and result <= 1.0
If all inputs are 0.0, result == 0.1 (operational floor)
If all inputs are 1.0, result == 1.0
Result is deterministic: same inputs always produce same output

invariants: All four component metrics (signal_frequency, author_seniority, channel_gravity, engagement_velocity) are always in [0.0, 1.0]
The default value for all component metrics is 0.5 (neutral/no-information sentinel)
The raw business_weight cached on Context is always in [0.0, 1.0] with default 0.5
The effective_business_weight is always max(business_weight, policy_floor) where policy_floor defaults to 0.1
effective_business_weight >= 0.1 under default configuration — no context is fully starved
compute_business_weight functions are pure: same inputs always produce same outputs, no side effects

Backward compatibility: existing Context instances without business_weight or business_weight_metrics deserialize successfully using Pydantic field defaults (business_weight=0.5, business_weight_metrics=BusinessWeightMetrics())
No migration scripts or schema version changes are required — this is a purely additive change
When all config weights are zero, compute_business_weight returns raw_weight=0.5 (the neutral default) to avoid division by zero
BusinessWeightMetrics is mutable (not frozen) — metrics are tracking state that updates over time
The sum of config weights need not equal 1.0 — the computation normalizes by dividing by the sum of weights
BusinessWeightComponents and BusinessWeightResult are frozen/immutable after construction for safe sharing across async boundaries
business_weight MUST NOT appear in any familiarity score computation, resonance check, or acceptance threshold evaluation — it affects evaluation ORDER only
Stop-on-first-accept semantics are preserved: business_weight changes which context is evaluated first, not whether a context is accepted
Routing snapshots are immutable: once created, ordered_contexts must not be re-sorted or mutated mid-round
Token budget allocation always sums to exactly total_budget (no tokens lost or created) using largest-remainder rounding
When floor allocations exceed total_budget, pro-rata reduction is applied so sum still equals total_budget
Priority queue ordering uses (-business_weight, insertion_counter) tuples to achieve descending weight order with stable FIFO tiebreaking
resolve_business_weight never raises on identity resolver failures; it falls back to default and records in defaulted_metrics
defaulted_metrics only contains values from the set {'signal_frequency', 'author_seniority', 'channel_gravity', 'engagement_velocity'}
